summary: Cuyamaca Peak lookout: 1918 timber tower, 1930s 30-ft steel K-brace tower, Forest Service use to 1975, demolished and burned in 1985.

facts.design: 30-foot steel K-brace tower (L-1600 series) with a 14-by-14-foot Region 5 live-in wood cab
facts.status_note: Demolished and burned in 1985 according to the register; the Descanso history says the lookout no longer exists

access.note: The summit lies inside Cuyamaca Rancho State Park and a popular hike reaches it; no source describes what remains on the summit

visit.trail_note: A popular year-round hike of about 3.5 miles runs from Paso Picacho Campground to the summit

events.note: First tower: a 10-foot enclosed timber tower with a 14-by-14-foot live-in cab
Replaced by a 30-foot steel K-brace tower. The register's Built field reads 'Circa 1930's', so the year is approximate
Peak incorporated into Cuyamaca Rancho State Park
A second lieutenant in the Marine Corps Reserve was killed when his plane crashed and set a brush patch on fire (August 1939); a forest lookout on the peak located the wreck
Lookout C.A. Brown trapped in his station for hours by a 74-mile-an-hour gale that held his outward-opening door shut (October 1939)
Lookouts Roy Pogue and Art Towne snowbound on the peak until a ski patrol relief party reached them (March 1944)
Register: the Cleveland National Forest operated the lookout through 1975; chapter says well into the 1970s
Register: demolished and burned. Chapter: burned in a wildfire or demolished by the mid-1980s
Registered February 17, 2009; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.proposed: built 1918 (first timber tower); replaced in the 1930s by the 30-foot steel tower
corrections.why: Both sources date the first tower to 1918. The register's Built field for the steel tower reads 'Circa 1930's', which is not an exact year, so 1930 should not be recorded as a build year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the chapter both date the first, timber tower to 1918. The register gives only a circa-1930s date for the steel tower that replaced it.
The register calls the cab a BC-301 design and the chapter calls it a C3. Both describe a 14-by-14-foot live-in wood cab on a 30-foot steel K-brace tower.
The register says it was demolished and burned in 1985. The chapter says it was burned in a wildfire or demolished by the mid-1980s. Both point to the mid-1980s; the cause is not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Register and chapter agree on the 1918 timber tower, the 1930s steel tower, the 1933 park incorporation and the mid-1980s loss, but disagree on the cab code (BC-301 vs C3) and the cause of loss. Brief's '1930 built' was rounded from the register's 'Circa 1930's'. Access set to public from Wikipedia's hike description, a secondary source; the brief had unknown. Staffing items for 1939 and 1944 come from a lookout history site quoting old newspapers; the newspapers themselves were not checked. No photo added: no image URL with a verified licence.
